title: Should you aim for MBB, the Big Four, or both?
description: A practical way to decide where to apply: the work you want, the interview formats, your background and why applying broadly is usually wise.
hook: Many candidates feel that anything other than MBB is second best. That view leaves a lot of great careers on the table. The better question is which kind of work and which firm suit you, and how to give yourself several good chances rather than one.
body:
Start with the work you want

  • If you want short, high-level strategy projects, target MBB and the Big Four strategy arms (Monitor Deloitte, Strategy&, EY-Parthenon) and firms like Oliver Wyman or Kearney.
  • If you are drawn to technology, transformation or implementation, the Big Four and Accenture have some of the biggest and best practices.
  • If you love one industry, look at firms known for it.

Think about your odds

MBB hires relatively few people from a very large applicant pool. Applying to a broader set of firms gives you more interviews, and more interviews make you better at interviewing. Many people move between firms later in their careers.

Prepare for the formats

MBB interviews centre on individual cases and deep fit questions. Big Four processes often add online tests, video interviews, group cases or presentations. If you apply to both, practise working in a group as well as solo cases. How group and written cases work.

A sensible plan

  1. Make a list of 8 to 15 firms across groups, based on the work and city you want.
  2. Note each firm's deadlines and formats.
  3. Prepare the core skills once (cases, maths, fit stories), then add firm-specific practice.
  4. Use earlier interviews as practice for the ones you care about most.

Sources

  • Road to Offer: Big 4 vs MBB consulting
  • Simplify: MBB vs Big 4 vs boutiques

Checked November 2026.

Compare the work, not just the logos

Suppose you have two interviews: one for a generalist strategy team and one for a transformation programme that will run for eighteen months. The first may offer more varied problem types; the second may allow you to see whether an operating change actually improves results. Neither is automatically better. Your preference should follow the skills you want to build.

Ask prospective teammates for a concrete example of a recent project, your expected responsibility in the first six months and how often consultants rotate between sectors. Investigate whether the role is advisory, execution-heavy or a mixture, and whether you will get client exposure early.

The preparation overlap is substantial: logical structuring, quantitative analysis, concise storytelling and credible motivation. Add role-specific practice rather than building an entirely separate case-interview method for each brand. Rehearse one example that proves you understand the difference between recommending a change and delivering it.
